title: Thyme infusion for digestive spasm
subtitle: A warming herbal tea of Thymus vulgaris for intestinal cramping and bloating
excerpt: Thyme infusion is a hot tea of dried Thymus vulgaris herb steeped for 8 minutes, taken for intestinal cramping, bloating, and the spasmodic pain of IBS-type symptoms. Thyme has a carminative and mild antispasmodic action in the gut. One cup after meals or at the onset of cramping. Brewed fresh each time.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), thyme entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Thymus vulgaris L. and Thymus zygis L., herba (2012, EMA/HMPC/234453/2009), open access.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried thyme stores 12 months in a sealed tin. Brew each cup fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb that relieves gas, bloating, and intestinal cramping by relaxing the smooth muscle of the digestive tract and dispersing trapped gas. Thyme, fennel, and ginger are all carminatives.

content.text: Thyme infusion is a hot tea of dried Thymus vulgaris herb, steeped for 8 minutes and drunk warm after meals or at the onset of abdominal cramping. A traditional

, used in European home herbal practice for intestinal spasm, bloating, and the crampy, irregular bowel pattern comes with IBS-type conditions. The same aromatic oils that give culinary thyme its flavour, thymol and carvacrol, act on the smooth muscle of the gut to reduce spasm and disperse gas. The taste is warm, aromatic, and slightly medicinal. One cup after meals.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 1 teaspoon of dried thyme in a teapot or heatproof cup. Pour 200 ml of just-boiled water over the herb. Cover.
Steep for 8 minutes. Covering is important, thyme's aromatic oils evaporate quickly and are part of the therapeutic action.
Strain into a cup and drink warm. Honey may be added.
One to three cups daily, taken after meals or at the onset of cramping. For ongoing IBS-type symptoms, up to three cups daily for 4 weeks then reassess.
Dried thyme stores 12 months in a sealed tin. Brew each cup fresh.
When not to use this remedy

See a doctor for abdominal pain that is severe, persistent, comes with blood in the stool, or accompanied by unexplained weight loss. These symptoms need diagnosis before symptomatic herbal treatment.
